thread:
Alex C: i'm taking primary for the 22:00-06:00 shift. quick note — we've been seeing noisy SLO alerts for inference.error_rate.p99 across hosts in eu-west. i bumped the alert threshold from 0.8% -> 1.5% to cut down on pages while i dig in. leaving details/runbook below, please ack if you're secondary.

Maria P: acked. thanks for the heads up. any customer-facing impact expected at that threshold?

Alex C: short answer: unlikely for most customers. the spike correlates with a batch of retrain jobs hitting the cluster and causing transient RPC failures. SLA risk is low for now but i'll keep an eye. if it moves above 2.5% we'll escalate to incident.

Jordan S: fwiw, we should log the threshold change for audit and ops. can you paste the exact alert rule and the reason? i'll update the audit doc.

Alex C: good call. pasted snippet from alert-manager:
```
alert: InferenceHighErrorRate
expr: sum(rate(inference_error_total[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[5m])) > 0.015
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: warning
annotations:
  runbook: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/inference-error-rate
```
Changed from `> 0.008` to `> 0.015` at 2026-03-14T22:03Z by Alex C (temp). Reason: correlated retrain batch causing spikes, noisy pages; monitoring window + canary planned.

Lee H: also add note to the shift-handoff log and mark that this is a temporary suppression until 06:00. i'll keep secondary on rotation.

oncall-bot: Pager sent to @eng-oncall-primary and @eng-oncall-secondary for alert InferenceHighErrorRate (severity: warning).

Maria P: quick QA: are we still routing fallback model variants when latency/err spikes? want to ensure user traffic degrades gracefully.

Alex C: yes — traffic fallback policy to small-quantized variant is active. I checked the routing logs; fallbacks increased ~4x during the peak but latency stayed within 95th percentile SLO.

Jordan S: thanks. i'm going to add a short customer-impact note to the incident tracker: "no functional regressions observed; temporary increase in fallbacks; no SLA breach so far." will flag if anything changes.

Alex C: runbook pointers for folks jumping in:
- primary: follow runbook steps 1-4 (investigate request/host map, check retrain job schedule, tail inference logs).
- secondary: monitor alerts, confirm pages, prep rollback for retrain if root cause points there.
Link: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/inference-error-rate (see TL;DR at top).

Maria P: if you need temp suppression beyond 06:00, propose we do a quick triage call before extending. prefer not to leave thresholds changed without sign-off.

Alex C: agreed. plan: continue observation till 02:00Z, if noisy but no increased customer impact i'll keep suppression until 06:00 then notify oncall rotation & infra owners. if error rate trends upward and customer errors rise, escalate immediately to P1.

Lee H: also adding a note: alert-manager annotation now includes `suppress_reason: transient training noise` and `suppress_owner: Alex C`. good for post-mortem.

oncall-bot: Note added to alert history by Alex C: "temp threshold bump to 1.5% due to retrain-induced noise; will review by 06:00Z."

Jordan S: one more operational nit — please include exact grafana dashboard panel id in the handoff note (makes retrospective easier).

Alex C: will do. panel: inference -> error-rate -> panelId=42.

Maria P: ack, i'll cover any customer comms if required. thanks for the clear notes.

Lee H: ack, i'm secondary and available if pages come back.

Alex C: thanks team — i'll post an update if anything changes or before extending the suppression.
